name: Empire in Flames Exploration
summary: The exploration chart for the wilderness of the Empire. Warband members taken out of action in the game may not take part in any of the encounters below: they gain no Experience, may not attack, and cannot be taken out of action by an encounter either. Attacking the Empire Huntsmen, Empire Patrol, Halfling Rangers, Holy Man, Large Farm, Lost Children, Mordheim Refugees, Peddler, Pilgrims or Small Farm carries a further consequence: roll a D6, and on a 1-3 the warband was careless and left witnesses, so the next time it rolls that exploration result, treat the encounter as (1 1) Abandoned Farmhouse instead.
income_note: Wherever the rules say wyrdstone, read Treasure: wyrdstone shards, small items of art, jewellery made of precious metals and set with gems, or merchant goods. Treasure acts exactly as a wyrdstone shard does and is sold on the rulebook's chart, which this chart keeps.

places.name: Abandoned Farmhouse
places.rules: Sifting through the smouldering ruins of a burned-out farm, the warband finds D6 gc.

places.name: Raving Lunatic
places.rules:
The warband may question the madman or kill him.
Undead warbands who kill him gain a Skeleton or Zombie at no cost.
Chaotic or Lizardmen warbands may sacrifice him to their Dark Gods and the warband leader gains 1 Experience.
Any other warband may question him; roll a D6:
1-4 He knows nothing.
5-6 He knows a secret tunnel to untold riches: in the next battle the warband may set up three of its members anywhere on the battlefield that is within cover and not within 10" of an enemy warrior. All three must start in the same general area, within 4" of one another.

places.name: Lost Children
places.rules:
The warband may help the two lost children find their parents. If it does, the grateful parents give the warband all they have of value: D6 gc, or a single Treasure instead if the roll is a 6.
Undead, Chaotic or Lizardmen warbands may instead sacrifice the children to their Dark Gods (or simply feed on them) and the warband leader gains 1 Experience.

places.name: Mordheim Refugees
places.rules:
If the warband is Human (not Possessed), Elf (not Dark Elf), Dwarf (not Chaos Dwarf) or Halfling, the refugees beg for help and offer information about the lands nearby. Roll a D6:
1-3 The information is lies and useless.
4-6 The information is useful: the warband may roll one dice more than normal for exploration after the next game.
Any other warband may sacrifice the refugees to their Dark Gods (or simply feed on them) and the warband leader gains +1 Experience.

places.name: Burial Site
places.rules: In an open grave in the corner of a small graveyard lies a gold medallion speckled with what appears to be rust. It may be sold for D6 gc.

places.name: Wild Stag
places.rules: Any warband members with missile weapons may shoot at the startled stag. On a successful hit, at the warrior's base chance to hit, and a wound against Toughness 3, the stag falls and the warband may have a feast. The next time the warband sells Treasures it counts as one size band lower (a warband of 10-12 members counts as 7-9), as it has to buy less food to re-supply.

places.name: Orc Encampment
places.rules:
A Greenskin warband may approach and attempt to trade. Roll a D6: on a 1 the Orcs fail their Animosity test and attack, following the rules for other warbands fighting the Orcs below. If they do not attack, the Greenskin warband may buy any equipment at a 25% discount, rounding down and rolling for Rare items as normal, and may sell items to the Orcs for 10% more teef (gold) than normal, rounding up.
A warband that is not Greenskin may report the encampment to the local authorities for a 2D6 gc reward, or attack the Orcs.
Any warband that attacks the Orcs receives D6 Experience, divided among the Heroes that did not go out of action, and 2D6 gc in loot. Roll a D6 for each warband member: on a 1 or 2 that warrior was taken out of action and must roll for Serious Injuries as normal.

places.name: Gypsies
places.rules:
The warband may trade with the gypsies or attack them.
A warband that attacks them gains D3 Experience, split among its Heroes, 2D6 gc and D3 daggers.
A warband that trades may buy any item of equipment at a 20% discount: work out the price as normal, then subtract 20%, rounding up to the nearest gc. Rare items must still be rolled for as normal. At the end of trading roll a D6: on a 1-3 the gypsies have robbed the warband, and all unspent gold crowns and Treasures are lost.

places.name: Small Farm
places.rules:
If the warband is inclined towards good rather than evil, the young couple provides a fine meal: when working out the warband's next earnings from selling valuables, reduce its effective size by one band (10-12 warriors counts as 7-9), as it needs to spend less on food.
If the warband is evil or Chaotic it may kill the young couple and loot their farm, receiving 2D6 gc and reducing its warband size by one band as above.

places.name: Pilgrims
places.rules:
If the warband is inclined towards good rather than evil, the pilgrims show it a shortcut through the nearby marshes: in the next game the warband may choose sides and take the first turn, and if two warbands in the game have this benefit, roll off to see which one enjoys it. The pilgrims' leader is an Elder of his congregation and may remove a curse placed on a member of the warband.
If the warband is evil or Chaotic it may kill the pilgrims and take their measly possessions: D6 gc and a Holy Relic.

places.name: Abandoned Orc Village
places.rules: If the warband searches the tumbled-down huts it finds the village treasury buried under one of them: 2D6 gc and a few hundred teeth. If the warband is Greenskin (Orcs and/or Goblins) the amount of money is tripled, as the teeth are actually worth something to them.

places.name: Empire Patrol
places.rules:
If the warband is inclined towards good rather than evil, the patrol lets it pass with only minor questions and gives it the name of a fair merchant in the next town: the next time the warband equips, prices are reduced by 10%, rounding down.
If the warband is evil or Chaotic the patrol attempts to arrest it. At the end of a short fight the warband gains D6 Experience, D6 gc, D3 halberds, D3 swords and D3 handguns. Roll a D6 for each warband member: on a 1-2 that member was also taken out of action during the fight and must roll for Serious Injuries as normal.

places.name: Treasure Stash
places.rules: Digging up an odd pile of leaves earns the warband a small chest holding D6x10 gc.

places.name: Herdstone
places.rules:
The warband has discovered a Beastmen herdstone.
A warband that is not Chaotic in nature may deface the herdstone and sift the offerings at its base for valuables: the warband leader gains 1 Experience and the warband finds D3 Treasures.
A Chaotic warband may leave a small offering of 10 gc and worship at the altar, asking either for a curse to be removed (roll a D6: on a 4-6 the curse is removed) or to gain knowledge. If knowledge is sought, roll a D6:
1-3 One of the warband's Heroes has his mind filled with insight and is immediately taken out of action. If he survives the experience he gains a single Academic skill, whether or not he could normally take one.
4-6 D3 Experience, distributed at random among the warband's Heroes and Henchmen groups.

places.name: Peddler
places.rules:
The warband may trade with the peddler and his pair of pack mules: it may buy items at a 20% discount, rounding the price up to the nearest gc, and any Rare item may be searched for at -2 to the difficulty, though he will only ever have one such item.
If the peddler is attacked his mules are spooked and run off, though 3D6 gc worth of items drop from their overladen packs as they leave.

places.name: Gingerbread House
places.rules: The warband may take some of the gingerbread to re-supply: it counts as two size bands lower when selling back Treasures (a warband of 10-12 members counts as 4-6), and any hirelings charge only half their normal upkeep. Roll a D6: on a 1-2 the old hag who lives in the house sees this and casts a powerful curse at the warband. Until the curse is removed, members of the warband must re-roll all successful hits in close combat or shooting.

places.name: Wounded Warband
places.rules:
If the warband helps the wounded warriors, they give it their stash: 2D6 gc and D3 Treasures.
If the warband dispatches them instead it gains D6 gc and the warband leader gains 1 Experience.

places.name: Empire Huntsmen
places.rules: If the warband is Human (not Possessed), Elf (not Dark Elf), Dwarf (not Chaos Dwarf) or Halfling, the huntsmen offer to show it a secret way through the woods to an area reputed to be ripe with treasure, and with danger: the warband may pick the next scenario, choose the table edge and take the first turn. If two or more warbands have this bonus, roll to see who the huntsmen showed the way to first.

places.name: Large Farm
places.rules:
If the warband is inclined towards good rather than evil, the farmer and his wife feed it a fine meal: when working out the warband's next earnings from selling valuables, reduce its effective size by two bands (10-12 warriors counts as 4-6), as it needs to spend less on food. The farmer also gives the warband the name of an honest merchant: the next time the warband buys equipment, prices are reduced by 20%, rounding the price up to the nearest gc.
If the warband is evil or Chaotic it may kill the farmers and loot their farm, receiving 2D6 gc and D3 Experience distributed among its Heroes, and may reduce its warband size by two bands as above. Roll a D6 for every member of the warband if it attacks the farmers: on a 1 that member was taken out of action in the fight and must roll for Serious Injuries as normal.

places.name: Halfling Rangers
places.rules:
If the warband is inclined towards good rather than evil, the Halflings share their travelling rations: when working out the warband's next earnings from selling valuables, reduce its effective size by two bands (10-12 warriors counts as 4-6), as it needs to spend less on food.
If the warband is evil or Chaotic the brave little rangers attack. The warband receives D6 gc, D6 short bows, D6 daggers and D3 Experience, which may be distributed amongst its Heroes, and may reduce its warband size by two bands by eating the Halflings' rations as above. Roll a D6 for each member of the warband: on a 1-2 that member is shot full of holes, taken out of action in the fight and must roll for Serious Injuries as normal.

places.name: The Hanging Tree
places.rules: A weak plea for help comes from one of the cages hanging in the great oak. If the warband frees him, the Assassin (see the Mordheim Annual) offers his services to the warband for free: no hiring fee, though his upkeep is paid as normal after the first game. Among the bodies the warband also finds D6 gc hidden in boots and the like, D3 daggers and a Lucky Charm, obviously not working properly.

places.name: Dark Priest
places.rules: The Dark Priest may be killed, in which case the warband leader gains 1 Experience and an Unholy Relic. An Undead or Chaotic warband may instead seek his blessing, which removes all curses plaguing the warband.

places.name: Faerie Ring
places.rules:
A warband that is not Undead or Chaotic in nature may sleep in the ring of mushrooms and gain a restful night's sleep: any of its warriors who were taken out of action last game are automatically healed to full health, with no need to roll for Serious Injuries.
An Undead or Chaotic warband may destroy the faerie ring and receive D6 Experience, divided among its Heroes. The faeries then place a powerful curse on the warband: from now on, until the curse is lifted, roll twice for Serious Injuries for each warrior taken out of action and apply the lower result.

places.name: Ambushed Warband
places.rules: If the warband loots the arrow-riddled bodies it finds D3 swords, one suit of light armour, D6 daggers, D3 spears, D6 shields and 2D6 gc. Roll a D6: on a 5 or 6 the warband also finds a Treasure on one of the bodies.

places.name: Griffon Nest
places.rules: A Hero may climb the rocky spire to the nest and bring down eggs, one at a time; the nest contains five eggs. For each egg he wishes to steal he must pass an Initiative test to get up and another to get back down. If he fails the roll to get up, nothing happens. If he fails the roll to climb down he suffers D6 Strength 6 hits immediately and any egg he is carrying down is lost. Every time after the first that he attempts the test, roll a D6: on a 1 the parent Griffon has returned. If the warrior has just passed a test to get up to the nest he gets no more eggs and is immediately knocked off, suffering the falling damage above; if he was on the ground when the Griffon appeared he suffers no other ill effects. Either way, no more eggs may be recovered. Each egg recovered may be sold for 50+2D6 gc.

places.name: Sword in the Stone
places.rules: A Hero may draw the sword from the stone if he rolls equal to or under half his Strength, rounded down. Each Hero gets only one test, and only his base Strength is used: no drugs or magical effects apply. A Hero who draws the sword receives a magical sword. In a campaign, ask the referee whether he has a suitable sword to carry; otherwise it is +1 to hit and +1 to wound.

places.name: Dead Drake
places.rules: An enormous lizard lies pierced by a lance beside the broken body of a knight and his steed. The only salvageable dragon parts are shards of bone, but the knight's lance and sword are unbroken and will fetch a good price. All of it counts as D3+2 additional Treasures, which the warband may add to its hoard.

places.name: Chaos Icon
places.rules: Choose a Hero to place the strange golden amulet around his neck; one of them has to. That Hero is affected by the rules for frenzy from now on, and the frenzy is not removed if he is knocked down or stunned. At the start of each game roll a D6 for him: on a 1 he has heard the call of the Dark Gods working through the amulet and heads north for the Chaos Wastes, and is removed from the warband roster. The amulet carries a powerful curse, which must be lifted before the Hero can take it from his neck.

places.name: Holy Man
places.rules: If the warband is not Undead or Chaotic in nature, the ancient man reveals himself as a priest of Sigmar and offers to help the warband on its next adventure. He may either remove any curses afflicting the warband, or bestow a powerful blessing: after the next battle, roll twice for Serious Injuries for any injured warband member and the player chooses which result affects the warrior.

places.name: Familiar
places.rules: If the warband includes a spell-caster, he may take the large toad as an item of equipment. The familiar acts as a power focus and whispers secrets into the spell-caster's ears as he sleeps: while he retains it he gains an additional spell and +1 to the roll when casting his spells, cumulative with the Sorcery skill. A warband without a spell-caster does not interest the familiar, and it quickly hops away.
